title: Compactification and inseparable preparation of a marked relative curve
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime and let $Y_0$ be an affine integral excellent Noetherian scheme of finite dimension $n$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. Let $W$ be an integral affine excellent Noetherian scheme and $f_0:W\to Y_0$ a dominant finite-type morphism whose generic fibre is an integral curve. Let $Z_W\subset W$ be a nowhere dense closed subset and suppose its generic fibre is zero-dimensional or empty. There are an affine integral normal excellent Noetherian scheme $Y_1$ of dimension at most $n$, finite and dominant over $Y_0$, an integral excellent separated Noetherian scheme $P$, a proper dominant morphism $f:P\to Y_1$, an effective Cartier divisor $E\subset P$, an open subscheme $P^\circ\subset P$, and a proper surjective morphism $h:P^\circ\to W$ finite over a dense open and of generic degree prime to $\ell$. The maps to $Y_0$ commute; $P^\circ$ is dense; and $|E|\cap P^\circ=h^{-1}Z_W$. If $\eta_1$ is the generic point of $Y_1$, then $P_{\eta_1}$ is a smooth geometrically integral curve and $E_{\eta_1}$ is finite etale, possibly empty. The prime $\ell$ is invertible on all these schemes. Normal means having integrally closed local domains. Geometrically integral means integral after every field extension. The divisor $E$ is locally defined by one non-zero-divisor. Here generic degree means $[k(P):k(W)]$, with function fields the stalks at the generic points. All inverse-image equalities involving subsets are equalities of underlying sets.

Conventions for these notions: [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-weil-open-immersion], [def-pc-scheme-fibre], [def-sc-function-field], [def-sc-generic-point]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion.

source.place: Expose IX 1.3, printed p. 132, from affine compactification through blowup, finite radicial extension, normalization and Stein factorization. Use the reduced marked support after inseparable normalization and blow it up if necessary to retain an effective Cartier marking; on the smooth generic curve its reduced finite etale ideal is already invertible. For geometric normalization and etale residue fields, Stacks Tag 0BXT (varieties-lemma-finite-extension-geometrically-normal) and Tag 030R (algebra-lemma-make-separable).

proof.text: Write $Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $W=\operatorname{Spec}R$. Finite type gives finitely many generators of the $A$-algebra $R$, hence a surjection $A[x_1,\ldots,x_m]\twoheadrightarrow R$ and a closed immersion $W\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^m_{Y_0}$. Use [det-nagata-affine-opens-projective] to obtain the schematic closure $C\subset\mathbf P^m_{Y_0}$ and a dense open immersion $W\hookrightarrow C$, with $C\to Y_0$ proper. The scheme $C$ is integral: its space is the closure of the irreducible $W$, and its structure sheaf injects into the direct image of $\mathcal O_W$ by schematic density; on every nonempty open its section ring therefore embeds in the function field $k(W)$. In particular its affine rings are domains.

source.place: Expose IX 1.3, p.132, “Compactifiant f”; Stacks 01WA, morphisms-lemma-H-quasi-projective-open-H-projective.

proof.text: The scheme $C$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. It is excellent: its finite-type affine charts over the excellent ring $A$ are excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent], and [lem-trf-excellent-scheme-affine-cover] promotes this to every affine open. Write $f_C:C\to Y_0$ for the structural map. Put $B=Y_0$ and let $Z\subset C$ be the reduced closed subscheme supported on the closure of $Z_W$ [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. This closure omits the generic point and intersects $W$ in exactly $Z_W$, because $Z_W$ is closed in $W$. The integral generic fibre $C_\eta$ has the same function field as the dense open $W_\eta$; [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg] makes both dimensions one. The notation $B,C,Z$ is used in the next steps; the auxiliary component denoted $T$ there is different from the original $W$.

source.place: Expose IX 1.3, p.132; excellence of the compactification and closure of the marking.

proof.text: Put $k=\kappa(B)$ and $X=C_\eta$. This is a proper finite-type $k$-scheme by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b) and [def-weil-proper-morphism]. It is integral: over a nonempty affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset B$, an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset C$ has generic fibre $\operatorname{Spec}((A\setminus\{0\})^{-1}R)$; dominance gives injections $A\subset R\subset\kappa(C)$, so this is a nonzero domain with fraction field $\kappa(C)$, by [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]. These charts have the same generic point, that of $C$, so their union is integral. Its dimension is $1$ by hypothesis. The closed subset $Z_\eta$ omits this generic point because $Z\ne C$. Give all closed inverse images below their reduced induced structure [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme].

source.place: Exposé IX §1.3, p.132: generic-fibre normalization reduction; affine generic-fibre interpretation

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normalization-geonormal-insep] to $X$. Obtain a finite purely inseparable extension $k_1/k$ such that the normalization $N_1$ of $(X_{k_1})_{\mathrm{red}}$ is geometrically normal over $k_1$. By [lem-pc-homeo-pure-insep], $X_{k_1}$ is irreducible and has dimension $1$, so its reduction is integral of dimension $1$. By [lem-sc-normalization-exists], $N_1$ is integral, finite over that reduction, of finite type over $k_1$, and of dimension $1$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-geonormal-dim-one-smooth] makes $N_1$ smooth. We have not inferred anything about the boundary from this smoothness.

source.place: Tag 0BXT (lemma-finite-extension-geometrically-normal); ILO IX §1.3 p.132

proof.text: Let $D_1\subset N_1$ be the reduced inverse image of $Z_\eta$. Its underlying set omits the generic point of $N_1$, since the normalization map and the purely inseparable projection send that point to the generic point of $X$. Hence [lem-pc-nowhere-dense-dim-zero] gives $\dim D_1\le0$, and [lem-pc-zero-dimensional-closed-subscheme-finite] makes $D_1$ finite over $k_1$. Its finite-dimensional coordinate algebra is Noetherian (chains of ideals are chains of subspaces), so [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes] gives finitely many irreducible components. Apply [lem-pur-finite-inseparable-geometric-reduction] to $D_1$ to obtain a finite purely inseparable $K/k_1$ such that $D=(D_1\times_{k_1}K)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is geometrically reduced over $K$. It is finite over $K$: base change preserves finite morphisms [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange], and reduction is a closed immersion, hence finite [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite]; compose these finite morphisms.

source.place: Tags 04KT (lemma-finite-extension-geometrically-reduced), 06LH (lemma-algebraic-scheme-dim-0); ILO IX §1.3

proof.text: Write $D=\operatorname{Spec}H$, with $H$ finite-dimensional and geometrically reduced over $K$. It is Noetherian, because ascending chains of ideals are ascending chains of finite-dimensional subspaces. Each nonzerodivisor $h\in H$ is a unit: multiplication by $h$ is injective, hence surjective on the finite-dimensional space $H$, so $hx=1$ for some $x$. Thus $Q(H)=H$. The minimal primes form a finite list by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-noetherian-total-ring-fractions]: its canonical decomposition of $Q(H)$ identifies $H$ with a finite product $\prod_j E_j$ of fields. Each projection is surjective, so $E_j$ is finite-dimensional over $K$. For any extension $\Omega/K$, $E_j\otimes_K\Omega$ is a direct factor of the reduced ring $H\otimes_K\Omega$, so is reduced. Each $E_j/K$ is separable: if $\alpha\in E_j$ were inseparable, its minimal polynomial would have a repeated root over an algebraic closure $\overline K$; hence $K[\alpha]\otimes_K\overline K$ would contain a nonzero nilpotent, which remains nonzero in $E_j\otimes_K\overline K$ since tensoring an injection of vector spaces is injective. By [lem-sc-finite-etale-algebra-criterion], $D$ is finite etale over $K$. If $H=0$, the product is empty and the same criterion applies.

source.place: Tags 02LX (lemma-total-ring-fractions-no-embedded-points), 00EU (lemma-minimal-prime-reduced-ring); finite-etale criterion

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-normalization-inseparable-base-change] for $X$, $k_1/k$ and $K/k_1$. Its hypothesis is the geometric normality from Step 4. It identifies the normalization $N$ of $(X_K)_{\mathrm{red}}$ with $N_1\times_{k_1}K$, over $X_K$, and identifies the reduced inverse image of $D_1$ with $D$. Reduced inverse images depend only on the underlying closed sets [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], so $D$ is exactly the reduced inverse image of $Z_\eta$ in $N$. The scheme $(X_K)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is integral of dimension $1$ by [lem-pc-homeo-pure-insep]; [lem-sc-normalization-exists] therefore gives $\dim N=1$. The normalization comparison makes $N$ geometrically normal, so [lem-weil-pbc-geonormal-dim-one-smooth] makes it smooth. Here $K/k$ is finite purely inseparable (degrees multiply, and in positive characteristic one multiplies the exponents that put elements into the bottom field).

source.place: Tag 0C3N (lemma-normalization-and-change-of-fields); ILO IX §1.3, preservation after the second extension

proof.text: Construct $b_1:B_1\to B$ as the normalization of $B$ in $K$ [def-fin-normalization-extension]. On a nonempty affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset B$, its coordinate ring is the integral closure $A'$ of $A$ in $K$. The field of fractions of $A$ is $k$ [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]. Excellence implies Nagata by [lem-exc-quasi-excellent-nagata]; taking the prime $(0)$ in [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] and then applying [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] says exactly that $A'$ is finite over $A$. Thus $b_1$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal], $A'$ is a normal domain with fraction field $K$. These rings glue by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization]. The resulting scheme is integral: all nonempty charts contain the common point with field $K$. Localizing $A'$ by $A\setminus\{0\}$ gives the integral closure of $k$ in $K$, namely $K$. Hence $b_1^{-1}(\eta)=\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $b_1$ is dominant.

source.place: Tags 032R (definition-nagata), 032F (definition-N), 034L (lemma-integral-closure-in-normal), 0307 (lemma-integral-closure-localize); ILO IX §1.3

proof.text: Each finite $A$-algebra $A'$ in Step 8 is excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]; [lem-trf-excellent-scheme-affine-cover] then gives excellence on every affine open of $B_1$. Since $b_1$ is finite, it is of finite type, so $B_1$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. It is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], and surjective: its image is closed by properness and dense by dominance. Thus $b_1$ is an alteration, in fact finite everywhere. This construction used no affine, projective or separated structure on the whole of $B$.

source.place: Tag 07QU (lemma-finite-type-over-excellent); morphisms Tags 01T6, 01WN

proof.text: Form $V=C\times_B B_1$, with projections $p:V\to C$ and $q:V\to B_1$. Let $\xi$ be the generic point of $C$. The fibre $p^{-1}(\xi)$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(C)\otimes_k K)$, since $b_1^{-1}(\eta)=\operatorname{Spec}K$. By [lem-pc-homeo-pure-insep] it has one point $z$. A generization of $z$ in $V$ must still map to $\xi$, so is $z$. Since schemes are sober [lem-sc-scheme-sober], $\overline{\{z\}}$ is an irreducible component: the generic point of any larger irreducible closed set would generize $z$. Let $T$ be its reduced induced closed subscheme [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. It is integral, dominates $C$, and dominates $B_1$, because $z$ maps to the unique point of $b_1^{-1}(\eta)$.

source.place: Tags 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober), 01J3 (lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme); ILO IX §1.3, dominant component

proof.text: The map $p$ is finite by base change of the finite $b_1$ [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange]. The inclusion $T\hookrightarrow V$ is finite [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite], so $T\to C$ is finite by the composition clause of [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange]. Hence $T$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Over the excellent affine charts of $C$, its coordinate rings are finite algebras, hence excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]; these cover $T$, so [lem-trf-excellent-scheme-affine-cover] makes $T$ excellent. Also $q$ is proper by base change of $f_C$ [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b); thus $T\to B_1$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](b).

source.place: Tags 01WL, 01WK (finite base change/composition), 035C (closed-immersion-finite), 01W4, 01W5; more-algebra Tag 07QU

proof.text: Normalize $T$ in its function field $F$, obtaining $n:C_1\to T$ [def-sc-normalization]. For every nonempty affine $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset T$, the integral closure $\overline R^{\,F}$ is finite over $R$: excellence gives Nagata [lem-exc-quasi-excellent-nagata], and the definitions [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring, def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] apply to the degree-one extension $F/F$. It is a normal domain with fraction field $F$ [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal]; the affine description therefore makes $C_1$ integral and $n$ finite and dominant. Its finite affine chart algebras are excellent [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent, lem-trf-excellent-scheme-affine-cover], and it is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Put $a_1=pn:C_1\to C$ and $f_1=qn:C_1\to B_1$, where $p,q$ are restricted to $T$. The first is finite by [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange]; the second is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](c). Both are dominant from the common generic point; $a_1$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper] and surjective by closed dense image. Thus $a_1$ is an alteration and $f_Ca_1=b_1f_1$.

source.place: Tags 032R, 032F, 034L; more-algebra Tags 07QV, 07QU; ILO IX §1.3 total-space normalization

proof.text:
Let $\eta_1$ be the generic point of $B_1$. By fibre-product associativity, $V_{\eta_1}=X_K$. This fibre is irreducible by [lem-pc-homeo-pure-insep]. The point $z$ is its generic point, since it has no proper generization in $V$ (Step 10). The closed subscheme $T_{\eta_1}$ contains $z$, so has its whole underlying space; it is reduced, since its affine rings are localizations of the domains on $T$. The uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] identifies $T_{\eta_1}=(X_K)_{\mathrm{red}}$. To compute $(C_1)_{\eta_1}$, take $\operatorname{Spec}A'\subset B_1$ and an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset T$ over it; put $S=A'\setminus\{0\}$. Dominance makes the image of $S$ nonzero in $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization],
$$S^{-1}(\overline R^{\,F})=\overline{S^{-1}R}^{\,F}.$$
The fraction field remains $F$. These equalities agree on overlaps, and the normalization definition [def-sc-normalization] identifies $(C_1)_{\eta_1}$ with the normalization $N$ of $(X_K)_{\mathrm{red}}$, compatibly with its map to $X$. Thus its generic curve is the smooth integral curve of Step 7.

source.place: Tag 0307 (lemma-integral-closure-localize); morphisms Tag 035K; ILO IX §1.3 generic-fibre identification

proof.text: Let $Z_1=(a_1^{-1}Z)_{\mathrm{red}}$. It omits the generic point of $C_1$, since that point maps to the generic point of $C$, so it is nowhere dense. Under Step 13, its generic fibre is $D$ from Step 7. Indeed both are the reduced closed subscheme in $N$ on the inverse image of $Z_\eta$. Reduction commutes with this generic localization: for a ring $R$ and multiplicative set $T$, if $r/t$ is nilpotent in $T^{-1}R$, some $u\in T$ kills $r^m$, so $(ur)^m=0$ and $r/t=(ur)/(ut)$ comes from the localized nilradical. The reverse inclusion is immediate. Use the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] for the resulting closed subschemes. By Step 6, $(Z_1)_{\eta_1}=D$ is finite etale over $K$.

source.place: Localization of nilradicals (written out); ILO IX §1.3 reduced inverse image

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-stein-smooth-generic-curve] to $f_1:C_1\to B_1$. Steps 9, 12 and 13 verify all its hypotheses: the schemes are excellent integral Noetherian, the morphism is proper dominant, and its generic fibre is a smooth irreducible curve of dimension $1$. It gives an excellent integral Noetherian $B_0$, a finite dominant $q_0:B_0\to B_1$, and a proper map $g:C_1\to B_0$ with $f_1=q_0g$. Its generic fibre is smooth and geometrically integral of dimension $1$, and $L=\kappa(B_0)=H^0(N,\mathcal O_N)$ is finite separable over $K$. The map $g$ is dominant: the generic point of $C_1$ maps into the generic fibre of $q_0$, whose sole point is the generic point of $B_0$, as checked next.

source.place: Exposé IX §1.3, p.132: Stein factorization

proof.text:
The fibre of the finite dominant map $q_0$ above $\eta_1$ is $\operatorname{Spec}L$: on an affine $\operatorname{Spec}A'\subset B_1$, its inverse image is $\operatorname{Spec}R_0$ for a finite domain $R_0$ with fraction field $L$ [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]. Localizing at $A'\setminus\{0\}$ gives a finite-dimensional domain over $K$, hence a field (multiplication by any nonzero element is injective and therefore surjective). Its fraction field is $L$, so it is $L$. Associativity of fibre products now gives
$$C_1\times_{B_0}\operatorname{Spec}L\cong C_1\times_{B_1}\operatorname{Spec}K=N.$$
Likewise $(Z_1)_{\eta_0}$ is the same scheme $D$ with its induced $L$-structure, not the generally larger scheme $D\times_K L$. These identifications use the finite map, integrality, function field and factorization supplied by [lem-trf-stein-smooth-generic-curve].

source.place: Exposé IX §1.3, p.132: generic fibre after Stein factorization

proof.text: The decomposition $H=\prod_jE_j$ in Step 6 is by quotient maps, so the $L$-algebra structure of $H=\Gamma(D,\mathcal O_D)$ from Step 16 induces maps $L\to E_j$. For each nonzero field factor this is an injection. Each $E_j$ is finite over $L$, since a finite $K$-spanning set is also an $L$-spanning set. It is separable over $L$: the minimal polynomial over $L$ of any $\alpha\in E_j$ divides its separable minimal polynomial over $K$, and a divisor of a square-free polynomial is square-free. Consequently [lem-sc-finite-etale-algebra-criterion] makes $(Z_1)_{\eta_0}$ finite etale over $L$. The empty product gives the empty boundary, also allowed by that criterion.

source.place: Separable finite extensions under an intermediate field; finite-etale product criterion

proof.text: Set $Q=C_1$ and $Y_1=B_0$, with structure map $g:Q\to Y_1$. The map $a_1:Q\to C$ constructed above is finite and surjective, and $Y_1\to B_1\to B=Y_0$ is finite dominant [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange]. Both bases are affine, since a finite morphism is affine [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The finite proper base map has dimension $\dim Y_1=\dim Y_0=n$ by [lem-trf-closed-dominant-dimension]. Its excellence, integrality and Noetherianity were established above and by the Stein statement. The generic fibre of $g$ is the smooth geometrically integral curve of Step 15, and the reduced marking $D=Z_1\subset Q$ is nowhere dense with finite etale generic fibre by Steps 14 and 17. All constructions are over $Y_0$.

source.place: Exposé IX §1.3, p.132: assemble finite normalization and Stein alterations

proof.text: The scheme $Q$ is normal by its construction as the normalization of $T$. Apply [lem-sbc-normal-sections-finite-product] to the quasi-compact open $Q$ of itself. The global section ring $H=\Gamma(Q,\mathcal O_Q)$ is a finite product of normal domains. It is a nonzero domain because restriction embeds it into $k(Q)$, so the product has exactly one nonzero factor and $H$ is integrally closed. By the relative-spectrum description in [lem-trf-stein-smooth-generic-curve], the affine scheme $Y_1$ is $\operatorname{Spec}H$. Localizations of $H$ are integrally closed by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization] applied to its integral closure in $\operatorname{Frac}H$. Thus every local ring of $Y_1$ is a normal domain, as required.

source.place: Expose IX 1.3, p.132, normal affine base after Stein factorization; Stacks 033H, normal sections.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal I_D$ be the reduced defining ideal of $D=Z_1$ and blow it up: $b:P=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_D}Q\to Q$. It is proper by [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper]. It is integral and birational: the chart cover [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover] and [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring] consists, after discarding empty charts, of subrings $R[I/a]\subset\operatorname{Frac}R$ for nonzero $a\in I$ in affine domains $R\subset k(Q)$. Every chart has the same generic point and field $k(Q)$, and away from $D$ the ideal is the unit ideal, so the map is an isomorphism by [cor-nagata-blowup-cartier-iso]. The charts are finite-type over excellent Noetherian charts of $Q$; [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent], [lem-trf-excellent-scheme-affine-cover] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] give excellence and Noetherianity. Put $E=V(\mathcal I_D\mathcal O_P)$. By [det-nagata-boundary-divisor-cartier], $E$ is an effective Cartier divisor with support $b^{-1}|D|$.

source.place: Expose IX 1.3, p.132, Cartier marking; Stacks 01OF, 02OS and 02ND, divisors lemmas on blowups.

proof.text: On the generic curve $Q_{\eta_1}$, the reduced finite closed subscheme $D_{\eta_1}$ has invertible ideal. Indeed, at any of its points the local ring is a one-dimensional Noetherian normal local domain (the generic curve was geometrically normal before Stein and its underlying scheme is unchanged); it is a DVR by [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr]. The reduced ideal there is the maximal ideal, hence generated by a nonzero uniformizer. Away from its finite support the ideal is the unit ideal. Local generators give local trivializations of this coherent ideal. Blowup commutes with this generic localization by [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map] and [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change]; the generic base-change map is flat since on affines it is localization by nonzero elements of the base domain. By [cor-nagata-blowup-cartier-iso], $P_{\eta_1}\cong Q_{\eta_1}$, and $E_{\eta_1}=D_{\eta_1}$ as closed subschemes. Thus the curve stays smooth geometrically integral and its marking is finite etale, including the empty case.

source.place: Expose IX 1.3, p.132; Stacks 00PD, 0805 and 01OF, reduced marking on the normal generic curve.

proof.text: Take $P^\circ=(a_1b)^{-1}(W)$ and $h=(a_1b)|_{P^\circ}:P^\circ\to W$. This is a dense open, since $a_1b$ sends the generic point to that of $C$, which lies in $W$. The map $a_1b$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper] and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], so its restriction over $W$ is proper. It is surjective: $a_1$ is finite dominant and $b$ is proper birational, so each has closed dense image; base change to $W$ preserves surjectivity here. The total transform support is $|E|=b^{-1}|D|$, and $|D|=a_1^{-1}|Z|$, whence $|E|\cap P^\circ=h^{-1}Z_W$ because $|Z|\cap W=Z_W$. The composite $f=gb:P\to Y_1$ is proper dominant. It is separated over the affine scheme $Y_1$, which is separated over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ (on an affine $\operatorname{Spec}H$, the diagonal comes from the surjective multiplication map $H\otimes_{\mathbf Z}H\twoheadrightarrow H$), so $P$ is separated. The same permanence statement gives properness of $f$ and all commuting structural maps.

source.place: Expose IX 1.3, p.132, restrict the proper model to the original affine piece and compare the marked supports.

proof.text: The function field $F=k(Q)=k(P)$ is the residue field of $k(C)\otimes_k K$, with $k=\kappa(Y_0)$ and $K/k$ the finite purely inseparable extension. Since $K$ is generated by finitely many elements each having a characteristic-power in $k$, their images generate $F$ over $k(C)=k(W)$ and have the same powers in $k(C)$. Thus $F/k(W)$ is finite purely inseparable; finiteness also follows from [lem-weil-pbc-purely-inseparable-base-change-local-ring] with $A=k(C)$. In characteristic zero this extension is trivial by the definition of purely inseparable. In characteristic $p>0$, [lem-weil-pbc-purely-inseparable-pth-root-tower] expresses it as a tower of degree-$p$ extensions, so multiplication of bases gives $[F:k(W)]=p^r$. The invertible prime $\ell$ is different from $p$, and consequently this degree is prime to $\ell$. Stein factorization changed only the base and did not extend $F$.

source.place: Expose IX 1.3, p.132; Stacks 09HI (fields-lemma-finite-purely-inseparable), degree-p root tower for a finite radicial extension.

proof.text: To see that $h$ is finite over a dense open, choose a nonempty affine open $V\subset Q$ disjoint from $D$. The complement $Q\setminus V$ misses the generic point of $Q$. The finite map $a_1:Q\to C$ has only that generic point over the generic point of $C$: localizing its affine coordinate domain at the nonzero elements of a base domain gives a finite-dimensional domain, hence a field. Its closed image $a_1(Q\setminus V)$ therefore misses the generic point of $C$. Remove this image and intersect with $W$, obtaining a dense open $W_1$. Above $W_1$, $a_1^{-1}(W_1)\subset V$, where $b$ is an isomorphism, so $h|_{W_1}$ is the finite map $a_1|_{W_1}$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. Finally every constructed scheme maps to $Y_0$, so the image of the unit $\ell\in\mathcal O_{Y_0}$ stays a unit on it. This verifies all finiteness and invertibility clauses.
